title: SYSK Selects: How the Cannonball Run Worked
summary: SYSK Selects rerun of the October 2009 episode on the Cannonball Run, the illegal cross-country road race started by automotive journalist Brock Yates in 1971. The episode covers Yates's 1971 test drive from New York to Los Angeles, the Ralph Nader and national speed limit backdrop, the origins of the name from Cannonball Baker, the first official run in 1972 won by Yates and Dan Gurney in a Ferrari Daytona, later runs, the 1979 final race and its movie tie-in, Burt Reynolds's 1981 film, imitators, and the European Cannonball Run. The episode closes with hosts' fast-driving stories and listener mail.
topics: Cannonball Baker Sea to Shining Sea Memorial Trophy Dash

segments.title: Selects intro and opening banter
segments.summary: Chuck introduces the Selects episode on the Cannonball Run, and the hosts open with 1980-era banter about pop culture and the Burt Reynolds movie.

segments.title: Brock Yates and the national speed limit debate
segments.summary: The hosts describe Brock Yates as an automotive journalist and contrast his pro-speed attitude with Ralph Nader's safety advocacy after Unsafe at Any Speed. They note the 1970s national speed limit, which was set low partly in response to the oil embargo.

segments.title: Yates's 1971 New York to Los Angeles drive
segments.summary: In 1971 Yates drove a Dodge Van from New York to Los Angeles in 40 hours and 51 minutes, averaging about 70 mph, to show that good drivers in good cars could cover the interstates safely.

segments.title: Origins of the name: Cannonball Baker
segments.summary: The hosts explain the race name by describing Erwin G. 'Cannonball' Baker, a motorcycle endurance racer, and his NASCAR commissioner role. The Polish Racing Drivers of America's telegram challenge led to the first official run.
topics: Cannonball Baker Sea to Shining Sea Memorial Trophy Dash

segments.title: The first official run in 1972
segments.summary: The first official run began in New York at midnight in November 1972 with eight entries, including a Cadillac driven by hired drivers. Rules included a 24-hour window and a fee. Yates and Dan Gurney won in a Ferrari Daytona in 35 hours and 54 minutes, and the teams used speed strategies and collected speeding tickets.

segments.title: Later runs, commercialization, and the 1979 race
segments.summary: Later runs grew in entries and media coverage, with a corporate-sponsored entry and a 1979 race that Yates considered ending. Hal Needham then staged a final race as a basis for a movie, with notable entrants and stunts, and the winning Jaguar driven by Dave Heinz and Dave Yarborough.

segments.title: Imitators and the European Cannonball Run
segments.summary: The hosts discuss films and races that imitated the Cannonball Run, including Cannonball! and The Gumball Rally, and the European Cannonball Run, which is a timed-average event rather than a race.

segments.title: Hosts' fast-driving stories
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh share personal stories of fast driving, including a speeding stop in Georgia and a rushed drive to a movie in Vermont.

segments.title: Listener mail and Kiva plug
segments.summary: A listener shares a creepy house story, and the hosts plug a podcast and the Kiva team fundraiser.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts invite listeners to send in fast-driving stories and close the episode.
